SMTO-HTTP-0008 — This HTTP Connection's settings changed while SMTO was using it

GUID: 4c1b3303-65e0-4a58-bf06-6c5d698ef51c
Slug: http-connection-changed
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • Someone edited this saved HTTP Connection, or the Task moved to a different Gateway, after SMTO had connected with it, so SMTO stopped using the old settings. The request wasn't sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you or someone else recently edited this HTTP Connection, open it in Parameter Store and confirm the settings are the ones you want. SMTO will reconnect with whatever is saved now.
  2. Select Test connection. This shows the current settings work before SMTO uses them in the Task.
  3. Ask SMTO in the conversation to reconnect with this HTTP Connection and repeat the request. A fresh connection uses the current saved settings; the old one is no longer accepted.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reconnects and your request completes without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages this HTTP Connection. Don't keep editing the connection while a Task is using it; each change makes SMTO drop the connection again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The saved HTTP profile's digest or the Gateway identity no longer matches the configuration the run verified or captured, so the stale connection was rejected and run-owned sign-in state was discarded.

What this means

  • The saved profile digest or verified working profile no longer matches the connection's accepted configuration. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The saved profile digest or verified working profile no longer matches the connection's accepted configuration.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare current profile revision/digest with the retained recipe; do not reuse old authentication state across the change.

How to fix it

  • Reconnect with http.connect, or reuse the profile_key, against the current saved profile on the intended Gateway so a new connection_ref is verified. If the edit was unintended, restore the profile in Parameter Store first. Do not reuse the stale connection_ref.
  • Refresh or recreate the connection for the intended current profile and origin.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A newly validated connection is bound to the current intended profile.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
